source.value:
Consider the following ellipse: 

$$
\dfrac{x^2}{2}+\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1
$$

 

Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$ and that $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=\sqrt{2}$ on the curve at the point $(1,\sqrt2),$ find the value of $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}$ at that point.

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-10912

source.question: e-10912
source.value:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (x)+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{y}{2}) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=\sqrt{2},$ $x=1,$ and $y=\sqrt2,$ and solve $\dfrac{\textrm{d}x}{\textrm{d}t}.$  We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (1)+\sqrt{2}\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+1 & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

decisions.question: e-10900

source.question: e-10900
source.value:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3}-\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 3{x}^{2}-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{1}{y} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}=2$ and $x=1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}6-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{1}{y} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $y,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $x=1$ into the equation of the curve.

At the point where $x=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =1 \\ 1-\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =1 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =0 \\ y & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $y=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{1}{1} & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the section of the hyperbola 

$$
\dfrac{x^2}{3}-\dfrac{y^2}{2}=1
$$

that lies in the first quadrant. Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$ and that $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=-2$ on the hyperbola at the point where $x=3,$ find the value of $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}$ at this point.

source.question: e-10963
source.value:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{2x}{3})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot y & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=-2$ and $x=3.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{2\cdot 3}{3})-(-2)\cdot y & =0 \\ 2\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+2y & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-y.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We also want to substitute for $y$, but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $x=3$ into the equation of the hyperbola.   

At the point where $x=3,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{{3}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =2 \\ {y}^{2} & =4 \\ y & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used $y > 0$ since we're only interested in the first quadrant. 

Finally, substituting $y= 2,$ we get  

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-y \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
